# uplapse_monitor (Resource)

An Uplapse monitor: a check run on a schedule from one or more locations, alerting when it fails.

Settings this resource does not model (alerting conditions, authentication, TLS assertions, journeys...) can be managed in the app: updates read the stored monitor and change only the attributes below.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "uplapse_locations" "europe" {
  continent = "Europe"
}

# Website: HTTPS check from every European location.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "website" {
  name            = "Website"
  type            = "HTTPS"
  url             = "https://www.example.com"
  interval        = 60
  timeout         = 30
  expected_status = 200
  locations       = data.uplapse_locations.europe.locations[*].id
  tags            = ["prod", "web"]
}

# API with request settings. Header values are sensitive and stored encrypted.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "api" {
  name     = "Orders API"
  type     = "API"
  url      = "https://api.example.com"
  path     = "/v1/health"
  interval = 60

  request = {
    method           = "GET"
    follow_redirects = false
    verify_ssl       = true
    headers = {
      Authorization = "Bearer ${var.health_token}"
    }
  }

  alert_contact_group_ids = [12]
}

# The page must contain a word.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "shop" {
  name    = "Shop"
  type    = "KEYWORD"
  url     = "https://shop.example.com"
  keyword = "Add to cart"
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "ping" {
  name = "Edge router"
  type = "PING"
  url  = "edge.example.com"
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "smtp" {
  name       = "Mail server"
  type       = "TCP"
  url        = "mail.example.com"
  port       = 25
  tcp_expect = "220"
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "postgres_port" {
  name   = "Database port"
  type   = "PORT"
  url    = "db.example.com"
  port   = 5432
  paused = true
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "mx" {
  name            = "MX record"
  type            = "DNS"
  url             = "example.com"
  dns_record_type = "MX"
  expected_dns    = "10 mail.example.com"
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "certificate" {
  name                 = "Certificate"
  type                 = "TLS_CERT"
  url                  = "www.example.com"
  min_tls_days_left    = 14
  interval             = 3600
  track_config_changes = true
}

resource "uplapse_monitor" "domain" {
  name                 = "Domain registration"
  type                 = "DOMAIN_EXPIRY"
  url                  = "example.com"
  min_domain_days_left = 30
  interval             = 86400
}

# The domain's email authentication: SPF and DMARC, plus MTA-STS in enforce mode and an IP blacklist watch on its
# mail servers.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "email_auth" {
  name                  = "Email authentication"
  type                  = "MAIL_AUTH"
  url                   = "example.com"
  required_mta_sts_mode = "enforce"
  check_blacklists      = true
  interval              = 3600
}

# A mailbox server: TLS on IMAPS (port 993 by default) and its certificate. Add a username and password in the app
# (Advanced > Authentication) to check that logging in works too.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "imap" {
  name          = "Mailbox server"
  type          = "MAIL_SERVER"
  url           = "imap.example.com"
  mail_protocol = "IMAPS"
}

# A job that must report in once a day: call heartbeat_url when it finishes.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "backup" {
  name                    = "Nightly backup"
  type                    = "HEARTBEAT"
  interval                = 86400
  heartbeat_grace_seconds = 1800
}

output "backup_ping_url" {
  value     = uplapse_monitor.backup.heartbeat_url
  sensitive = true
}

# An AI agent that runs at least hourly: each run pings heartbeat_url with state=start, then state=success or
# state=fail with its tokens and cost. Alerts when runs stop, when 3 runs in a row fail, or when the last hour's
# runs cost more than 10 USD.
resource "uplapse_monitor" "support_agent" {
  name                           = "Support triage agent"
  type                           = "HEARTBEAT"
  interval                       = 3600
  heartbeat_grace_seconds        = 600
  agent_monitor                  = true
  agent_max_cost_per_hour        = 10
  agent_max_consecutive_failures = 3
  agent_cost_currency            = "USD"
}

variable "health_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Monitor name, unique within the organisation (up to 255 characters).
- `type` (String) Check type: `HTTPS`, `API`, `KEYWORD`, `PING`, `PORT`, `TCP`, `SSH`, `DNS`, `TLS_CERT`, `HEARTBEAT`, `DOMAIN_EXPIRY`, `MAIL_AUTH`, `MAIL_SERVER`, `CERT_TRANSPARENCY`, `JOURNEY`, `BROWSER`, `FORM`. `HTTPS` covers plain HTTP too; `API` is an HTTP check with request settings; `PORT` only connects, `TCP` also sends `tcp_payload` and expects `tcp_expect`.

### Optional

- `agent_cost_currency` (String) `HEARTBEAT`: with `agent_monitor`, the 3-letter currency code the agent reports `cost` in (display only, default `USD`).
- `agent_max_consecutive_failures` (Number) `HEARTBEAT`: with `agent_monitor`, a failed run only fails the monitor once this many runs in a row have failed (1-1000, alert source `agent_failure_streak`); earlier failures are recorded as `agent_run_failed` without an alert. Left out, every failed run fails the monitor, as for a job.
- `agent_max_cost_per_hour` (Number) `HEARTBEAT`: with `agent_monitor`, fail (alert source `agent_cost_ceiling`) when the cost of runs finished in the last 60 minutes exceeds this, in `agent_cost_currency`. Left out, cost is not limited.
- `agent_monitor` (Boolean) `HEARTBEAT`: the heartbeat tracks an AI agent. Pings may carry a run outcome, tokens and cost (`state`, `runId`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cost`, `model`); `agent_max_cost_per_hour` and `agent_max_consecutive_failures` are evaluated on every finished run. Counts against the plan's agent monitor limit.
- `alert_contact_group_ids` (Set of Number) Ids of contact groups alerted when the monitor fails. Left out, the groups chosen in the app are kept; set `[]` to remove them all.
- `alert_user_ids` (Set of Number) Ids of the organisation's users alerted when the monitor fails. Left out, the recipients chosen in the app are kept; set `[]` to remove them all.
- `check_blacklists` (Boolean) `MAIL_AUTH`: also fail when one of the domain's mail server addresses is on a public IP blacklist (SpamCop, Barracuda, PSBL, Mailspike, UCEPROTECT level 1, DroneBL).
- `dns_record_type` (String) `DNS`: record type to resolve: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `TXT`, `MX`, `NS`, `CAA`.
- `expected_dns` (String) `DNS`: answer the record must contain (MX answers are `"<preference> <host>"`).
- `expected_status` (Number) HTTP status code the response must have (100-599).
- `heartbeat_grace_seconds` (Number) `HEARTBEAT`: seconds of lateness tolerated after `interval` before the monitor fails (API default 60).
- `interval` (Number) Seconds between checks (1-86400). Defaults to the plan's shortest interval; a shorter one than the plan allows is refused by the API.
- `keyword` (String) Text the response must contain. Required for `KEYWORD`.
- `location_target_type` (String) Check from a broader area instead of listed cities: `COUNTRY` (value: country id), `CONTINENT` (value: continent name), `PRIVATE` (value: private location id), or `CITY` (value: city id).
- `location_target_value` (String) Value for `location_target_type`.
- `locations` (Set of Number) Ids of the cities to check from (see the `uplapse_locations` data source). Several cities are checked on every run. How many a monitor may use depends on the plan.
- `mail_protocol` (String) `MAIL_SERVER`: the protocol to check: `SUBMISSION`, `SMTPS`, `IMAP`, `IMAPS`, `POP3`, `POP3S`. The check reads the greeting, sets up TLS (STARTTLS on `SUBMISSION`, `IMAP` and `POP3`) and checks the certificate. With a username and password set in the app (Advanced > Authentication) it also logs in; it never sends or reads mail.
- `min_domain_days_left` (Number) `DOMAIN_EXPIRY`: fail once fewer days than this remain on the domain registration.
- `min_tls_days_left` (Number) `TLS_CERT`: fail once fewer days than this remain on the certificate.
- `path` (String) Request path kept apart from `url` (`API` and `KEYWORD` monitors). Must start with `/`.
- `paused` (Boolean) Pause the monitor: no checks and no alerts. The API refuses to pause a monitor that is down outside a maintenance window.
- `port` (Number) Port. Required for `PORT` and `TCP`; `HTTPS` monitors default to 443 or 80 from the URL scheme, `MAIL_SERVER` monitors to the protocol's port (587, 465, 143, 993, 110 or 995). Port 25 cannot be monitored.
- `request` (Attributes) HTTP request settings for `HTTPS`, `API` and `KEYWORD` monitors. When the block is left out, request settings made in the app are kept. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--request))
- `required_mta_sts_mode` (String) `MAIL_AUTH`: fail unless the domain publishes MTA-STS in at least this mode: `testing` or `enforce`. Left out, MTA-STS is reported but not required.
- `tags` (Set of String) Free-form tags.
- `tcp_expect` (String) `TCP`: text the response must contain. Without it a `TCP` check is just `PORT`.
- `tcp_payload` (String) `TCP`: data written after connecting.
- `timeout` (Number) Seconds before a check gives up (1-300, not longer than `interval`).
- `track_config_changes` (Boolean) Record DNS, TLS and security-header snapshots and report changes between checks.
- `url` (String) What to check: an `http(s)://` address for HTTP-family types, a host name for `PING`, `PORT`, `TCP`, `SSH`, `DNS`, `TLS_CERT`, `DOMAIN_EXPIRY` and `MAIL_SERVER`, a domain for `MAIL_AUTH`. Required for every type except `HEARTBEAT`. Hosts on internal networks are refused.

### Read-Only

- `heartbeat_url` (String, Sensitive) `HEARTBEAT`: the address your job calls to report in. Anyone with it can report, so it is sensitive.
- `id` (String) Monitor id.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED` (paused, by you or by a plan downgrade).

<a id="nestedatt--request"></a>
### Nested Schema for `request`

Optional:

- `body` (String, Sensitive) Request body.
- `follow_redirects` (Boolean) Follow redirects.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Request headers. Values are sensitive; the API encrypts them and never returns credential-bearing ones, so changes to those made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `method` (String) HTTP method (default `GET`).
- `user_agent` (String) User-Agent header.
- `verify_ssl` (Boolean) Fail on an invalid TLS certificate.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform 1.5+: import blocks.
import {
  to = uplapse_monitor.website
  id = "123"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a monitor by its id (shown in the app's address bar: /monitors/edit/<id>).
terraform import uplapse_monitor.website 123
```
